refusals.where: bars.json W4 (says, accept, meant.source); ambiguities.md item 7; owner_pages.md 'Mad grazers'
refusals.evidence: The frozen sheet design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_scarlands.md says in §4 that the plated grazer is 'guaranteed to lose its mind', and in §5 (Always true) that 'the plated grazers always succumb in the end'. W4 says 'a clean or successfully cured chatrak avoids that delayed onset'. RM_Warscar.xml sets wildAnimalScariaChance 0.5, so under W4 about half the wild plated grazers never turn. Ambiguity 7 and W4 credit this to a 'kit ruling'. The only source is the criterion 'A clean chatrak tames and never snaps' in infrastructure/state/items/closed/WARSCAR_SNAP_MARK_1.md. An agent wrote that build criterion; it is not an owner ruling. Nothing in the cast file's ruling table (warscar_bedazzle_cast_2026-09-30.md) separates clean animals from cured ones.
refusals.would_pass: W4 either agrees with §5 (for example: every wild plated grazer on the Warscar eventually shows the change unless the player treats it), or keeps the clean/infected split as an open owner question carrying the frozen-sheet evidence. The Evidence-for-Ask rule makes such a question legitimate here.
refusals.smallest_fix: Relabel W4's source for the clean/cure split as 'delegated', not a kit ruling. Add one question to page two: '§5 says plated grazers always succumb; the build arms only the half that carry scaria. Default: only scaria carriers turn. If you say otherwise, every wild chatrak arms.'

refusals.where: next_version.md 'mark'; census.json row mark; owner_pages.md page one
refusals.evidence: The frozen sheet says in §5 (Always true): 'Salvagers return changed — sick in body, marked in mind.' Its §7b names the Scarlands mark as the mind currency of the curse. refusals.would_pass: Either keep the bare mark (accrual, mood and nightmare, floor) as part of what being here costs, with a bar, and move only the trade bonuses and loosened panels; or move it with a specific deletion argument against §5 and the 'cursed' sentence, shown on his pages.
refusals.smallest_fix: In next_version.md, give the mark a specific deletion argument. Add one page-two line: '§5 marked in mind / cursed: deferred; 0.1.0 carries the curse only through toxic dust and mad grazers'. Make that line a question with the evidence.

refusals.head: cannot_hold_together
refusals.where: bars.json R2 and the 'ground' meeting; tickets.md T17; W2 against W3
refusals.evidence: R2 says 'Ordinary toxin/pollution paths' and T17 says 'the smallest ordinary pollution-source renewal on the saved native-substrate mask'. RM_WarscarFlora.xml sets no <pollution> on RM_Glower, RM_ScorchedStars or RM_WreckLichen. In vanilla the default is Pollution.CleanOnly (enum value 0; PlantProperties.RequiresNoPollution). On any polluted cell, Plant.DyingFromPollution kills such a plant, and PlantUtility refuses to place it ('MessageWarningPollutedCell'). So the renewal R2 and T17 prescribe would kill the crusts and lichen on the native ground where W3 says the grazers feed. The proposal marks the meeting 'unknown' and defers it to the season model, but reading the code already decides it.
refusals.would_pass: Either a rule that the native crusts tolerate pollution (pollution Any or PollutedOnly), with a C4 def check, or a renewal design that does not write vanilla cell pollution under them.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add to R2: 'native crust flora are pollution-tolerant'. Add the def field check to C4. Mark the ground meeting 'argued' for this pair.

refusals.head: evidence_cannot_tell
refusals.where: bars.json W9 (range.varies, range.left_out, meant 'stall'); same pattern in W5 range.left_out
refusals.evidence: W9 allows 'Natural wind trace and separate labelled complete-cycle replay' and 'No forced wind change on finite all-calm trace: report it then replay declared transition.' It defines a stall as 'eligible sustained calm/wind never closes the cycle'. A build whose thresholds the shipped tile's natural weather never reaches is then not a stall by that definition, and it passes on the forced replay. That is the same false pass as the Pyrelands scenes run with the sky forced.
refusals.would_pass: The natural, unforced season leg at shipped defaults must itself show at least one complete calm, fall, wind, lift cycle on the shipped weather. An all-calm or all-wind natural season counts as a W9 stall, a fail or UNMEASURED and re-run on natural weather, and is never cured by the replay. The replay stays as a diagnostic only.
refusals.smallest_fix: Rewrite W9's range/left_out and the 'stall' definition to drop 'eligible' and put the natural-cycle requirement in. Make the same change to W5's 'No guaranteed wind change' clause.

refusals.head: kept_mechanic_undefined
refusals.where: census.json row persistent_poison (built: absent, fate needed_by land); W2 accept picture; tickets.md T17; definition.md 'Costs and failure signs'
refusals.evidence: The only definition given is 'remains a source of contamination after local cleanup' / 'temporary clearing is possible, permanent ecological recovery is not'. It never says whether renewal reaches cells under player floors and roofs, what a pawn working on exposed native ground suffers from it (as distinct from W5's airborne dose), or what readable sign shows renewal happening. W2's accept picture ('Cleanup leaves useful floor for a roofed work area, while exposed native substrate remains a contamination source') can be built two ways: the base re-pollutes forever, or only open ground does. T17 hands all of this to a later spec.
refusals.would_pass: The definition states where renewal acts (exposed native mask only, or under floors too), what it does to pawns and plants there, and its readable sign. No numbers are needed.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one paragraph to definition.md and one ambiguity row choosing 'exposed native cells only; player floors and roofs stop renewal beneath them' (or the other reading), and reflect it in W2's pictures.

refusals.head: contradicts_ruling_or_lore

refusals.evidence: src/RimMandrake/Scarlands/Patches/Patches_BrokenTurretAim.xml adds CompProperties_TurretAim def-wide to AncientAutocannonTurret and AncientUraniumSlugTurret. RM_CompTurretAim.cs gates it only on RM_WarscarSettings.turretTrackingEnabled, with no biome check. The census itself notes: 'Patch is def-wide, so targets outside Warscar are affected too.' As proposed, this Warscar mechanic runs by default on every map that has those ancient turrets. Ambiguity 14 says only 'No promise of tracking on unrelated biomes', which is not a gate.
refusals.would_pass: Tracking defaults to Warscar maps only. Any off-biome tracking sits behind the existing unsupported cross-biome opt-in, off and labelled.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add a ticket (or extend T23) to gate CompTurretAim on the Warscar biome lookup, with an off-biome map in its acceptance test.

rounds.missed_capability: The census has no row for the biome's player-facing text: RM_Warscar.xml <description> and <settleWarning>. That text falls under the frozen sheet's §6 hard ban 1 (no §GM truth in player text). It also makes promises 0.1.0 no longer keeps: the settleWarning says 'The Forgotten Sentinels defend the ground; they do not pursue past their lines', and the description says 'machines defend the place'. The Sentinels belong to campaign_kit_data, which the proposal moves to the next version, off. T23's 'descriptions that currently promise deferred rewards' does not name the Sentinel promise and does not check the §GM leak ban.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: Three-way meeting: R2/T17 (renew native contamination through ordinary vanilla cell pollution) × W3 (crust grazers feed on glower, scorched stars and wreck lichen on the native floor) × vanilla Plant.DyingFromPollution / PlantUtility. Those three RM flora defs set no <pollution>, so they default to CleanOnly. Every renewal pulse then kills the food web's producers on the very cells the wreck-lichen seeder and wildPlants spawning refill. The result is a loop: renewal kills, the seeder re-seeds, renewal kills again. It ends in the W9 'desert' (unharvested habitat cannot support life), which W2 and W3 each pass alone. RM_Warscar.xml declares no pollutionWildAnimals, but WildAnimalSpawner reads world-tile pollution, not map cells, so animal spawning is not part of this loop.

rounds.missed_capability: Toxic surface water. The_scarlands.md §3 says 'Surface water rises here … and it kills you: … poisoned ponds', and the shipped settleWarning (RM_Warscar.xml:63) tells the player 'Water is toxic'. Tickets.md T08 asserts 'New maps retain ordinary poisoned-water dressing' once pools are off. The census has no row for it: only the moved pools/pool_reagents/pool_remains rows, with no evidence of what places non-pool toxic water. So whether that water exists at defaults, or disappears with the RM_ReactionPools genstep, is undefined. A smaller related gap: the biome row calls the sky 'dry toxic', but its weather list includes ToxRain (rainRate 1, with a 'Tox rain' letter), whose commonality is 0 on a zero-rainfall tile. Whether 'ordinary toxic weather', which W5 and W9 assume is running, ever occurs is unmeasured.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: R7 + W3 + W9, through vanilla Scaria. R7 makes every wild chatrak an ordinary Scaria carrier. Vanilla then forbids taming it (TameUtility.cs:51, Designator_Tame.cs:61), and when it is killed its corpse rots unbutcherable with probability scariaRotChance (Pawn.cs:3491-3493; 0.6 at the default difficulty, Difficulties.xml:128). Chatrak is the commonest edible grazer (0.25) beside the inedible tetchik (0.5). T26 removes forage, so humans must carry food or hunt it. W3 promises 'normal hunting, butchery and feasible taming'. Meanwhile every chatrak eventually rages, which W9 counts as a flood if it cascades. The life meeting names onset and mark interruptions but not Scaria rot or the taming ban, so the food-web model as specified would miss this three-way meeting. Inevitability could come from RM incubation alone without vanilla Scaria; that is the rule to attack first.
